title: Telemetry -> Heuristic Mapping for Optimize Recs (WIP)
content:
Notes (brain-dump) - objective: map telemetry signals to an actionable recommendations UI for Optimize. This is intentionally rough — capturing heuristics, sample wireframe text, and the initial grooming/prioritization for implementation.

Context and goals:
- Problem: product teams want one-click, low-risk prescriptions (batching, caching, quant) that materially improve cost/latency without breaking quality. Ops + eng want traceable heuristics so we can explain why we suggested changes.
- Goal: present recommendations derived from live telemetry (batch size distribution, avg latency, prefix/KV cache hit rate, p99 tails, token cost trends, model quantization compatibility) in a compact, trustable card list + details pane.

High level UX concept (center/right detail layout):
- Left rail: workload selector + quick filters (hosted/dedicated/private, model family, route, timeframe).
- Center: vertical stack of recommendation cards (ranked by estimated 7-day savings * confidence). Each card is 1 line summary + two small badges (estimated cost delta, est latency delta) + confidence pill. Click expands.
- Right details: telemetry mini-charts (time series for batch size, latency, tokens per request, kv cache hit %), simulation sliders (simulate larger batch sizes / enable prefix cache / apply quant profile) and a small A/B preview that shows sample responses: baseline vs simulated.

Recommendation card anatomy (copy + fields):
- Title (short): e.g. "Enable prefix caching for /api/v1/chat"
- Subtitle (why): one-line heuristic: "High prefix reuse (avg prefix similarity 78%) on 95th percentile routes"
- Badges: "-$0.021/1k tokens" (green), "-18ms p95" (blue)
- Confidence: low/medium/high (based on telemetry volume and historical sim accuracy)
- CTA row: [Simulate] [Preview] [Apply -> rollout modal]
- Microcopy: small line: "Non-destructive: changes are config-only; model outputs unchanged unless quantization applied."

Heuristic definitions (rough):
- Prefetch/prefix cache suggestion: trigger when prefix_similarity_avg >= 0.6 AND prefix_reuse_rate >= 0.25 AND requests_per_minute >= 10 for route-window. Confidence = min(telemetry_volume_score, historical_sim_match).
- Batching suggestion: trigger if observed avg_batch_size < suggested_batch_size_for_latency_SLO AND p95_latency variance < BATCH_SAFE_VARIANCE. Use current latency SLO to set upper bound. Warn if p99 increases in sim.
- KV-cache optimization: recommend TTL adjustments when kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.5 and repeated prefixes identified; suggest more aggressive KV retention for routes with > 60% contextual reuse.
- Quantization recommendation: recommend model variant q* when tokens_per_request_avg high and quality-regression risk low (derived from eval set). Must attach evaluation artifact: delta-BLEU/ROUGE or model-eval diff. Only recommend if quant-perf test passes historical delta thresholds.

Scoring & ranking:
- Score = weight_savings * est_usd_savings + weight_latency * est_latency_improvement_ms + weight_confidence * confidence_score. Tunable weights in product settings.
- Confidence calculation dimensions: telemetry_volume (scaled log), model_eval_coverage (how many eval prompts overlap), sim_accuracy_history (how often prior sims matched real recs).

Wireframe copy bits (used in prototype):
- Empty state: "No recommendations right now — try expanding the timeframe or selecting busy routes. We'll surface suggestions when telemetry shows clear win conditions."
- Apply modal title: "Apply recommendation: Enable prefix cache"
- Modal body microcopy: "This change will update routing/config for selected routes only. We'll run a canary (10% traffic) for 24 hours and auto-rollback on error or quality regression."
- Rollout knobs: canary % (10/25/50/100), duration (4h/24h/7d), monitor intents (latency, quality, error rate), metric triggers for rollback.

Simulations:
- Primary simulation types: offline sim (batch profiler sim using recent traces), short live canary sim (safe, read-only routing test with mirrored traffic), content-check sim (run a small eval set through quantized model).
- UI sliders: batch size slider (1..64), cache retention (seconds), quant profile dropdown (none, q4_0, q8_0, int8). Show instant est delta badges and confidence change.

Backlog grooming (prioritized, rough estimates):
- OPT-412: telemetry-to-heuristic mapping service (backend) — 5 pts — owner: Ethan. (needs telemetry schema doc + sample stream).
- OPT-428: recs UI cards + detail pane + simulation UX — 8 pts — owner: Maya. (mockups + accessibility pass).
- OPT-433: rollout modal + canary automation integration — 3 pts — owner: Rosa.
- OPT-440: quantization evaluation pipeline hook (attach eval artifact to rec) — 5 pts — owner: Liam.
- OPT-451: A/B preview generator service (baseline vs simulated diffs) — spike (2 pts) — owner: Maya (investigate privacy).
- TODO: add unit tests for heuristic thresholds, add telemetry feature flags.

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- How to ensure recommendations don't encourage unsafe quantization choices for customer-sensitive workloads? Need explicit policy layer (allowlist/denylist per org).
- Privacy: sim and preview must not leak user payloads. Use redaction or synthetic sampling.
- Regulatory: private deployments cannot send traces off-host. How to run offline heuristics? Provide an on-prem mapping binary or clear instructions.
- UX explainability: product needs "why this rec" link to telemetry query and small explainer. Keep it short and link to full confluence page.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Backend produces ranked recs for a given route with: title, estimated_savings_usd, est_latency_delta_ms, confidence_score, recommended_action (batch/cache/quant), supporting telemetry links.
- UI displays stacked cards, expands to details with telemetry charts and a simulation slider.
- Apply modal triggers canary rollout with preset knobs and records decision in audit log.
- Integration tests for offline sim must show simulated savings within +/- 30% of real impact in 3/5 historical samples.

Sample grooming notes (meeting 2026-02-15):
- Rosa: wants a mid-fidelity prototype before backend is fully done; suggested using mocked telemetry with 3 canonical workload types (short-chat, long-doc, search-rewrite).
- Ethan: flagged telemetry volume cold-start risk — add a fallback "heuristic dry run" that can still suggest conservative recs.
- Liam: noted quantization recommendations must include explicit model hash and PRNG seed for reproducibility of evals.

Next steps / action items (short):
- Maya: build clickable figma prototype for card/detailed pane (due: 2026-02-28).
- Ethan: draft telemetry schema + example payloads, post to confluence (due: 2026-02-25).
- Rosa: write canary rollback contract doc and post in linked_artifacts (OPT-433) (due: 2026-03-04).
- Liam: prototype small offline quant-eval harness and attach to github PR template.

Loose UX copy bank (for design handoff):
- Recommendation title variants: "Use prefix caching", "Increase batching on low-latency routes", "Use q8_0 variant for high-throughput"
- Short explanations: "We saw repeated context reuse — caching prefixes reduces token decoding by ~X%", "Bumping batch size yields unit cost improvement at small p95 cost to latency"
- Warning microcopy: "Quantization may change model outputs. Recommend running the provided eval set before rollout."

End notes: this doc intentionally mixes product-level heuristics with UX copy and grooming. Keep as canonical place for the initial handoff. Will split into separate Confluence pages and implementation tickets after prototyping.

Random todo bullets (notes-to-self):
- Add small inline "why we recommend" tooltip that shows exact telemetry query used.
- Add "re-run simulation" button that uses fresh traces.
- Audit trail: who applied, when, canary results snapshot.

-- Maya
